check: The first screen says who it is for, what changes for them and how, in plain words.
A stranger can say what the product does after five seconds on the first screen.
The hero artifact is the product or its real output, not decoration.
Each of the visitor's first three doubts is answered by a specific artifact on the page.
Every section tells the visitor something the sections above did not; repeated claims are cut.
There is one primary action, worded the same wherever it appears.
Questions to the user carried a recommended default; unanswered ones were assumed and logged.

Two hero variants that differ on one named axis (structure, density, emphasis, type or voice) were scored before code, one of them is the statement dealt and chosen for this product, and neither is the category's obvious default or the obvious "anti-default".
Two references serve different jobs, one counterexample is named, what is not borrowed is stated, and departures from the chosen recipe are recorded.
The h1 has 3–12 words and says more than the product or company name.
A subhead of one or two sentences, at most 40 words, follows the h1 and is visible without scrolling.
The first screen says what kind of thing the product is: a plain category noun or an "X for Y" frame.

The record names the visitor's current alternative (including doing nothing), the one advantage only this product has, the category frame, and who it is for and not for; the headline would be false or odd on the alternative's page.
Every headline and section heading passes two of three tests: a reader can picture it, it could be proven false, it would not fit a named competitor's page unchanged.
The record lists at least three phrases in the target users' own words with their source, or says none exist yet; the hero uses or adapts one.

The first screen contains none of the generic marketing phrases on the list (for example seamless, supercharge, unlock, unleash, streamline, effortless, all-in-one, next-gen, cutting-edge, revolutionize, "AI-powered", "not just X, it's Y", "say goodbye to").
No superlative (best, #1, leading, fastest, world's first, unmatched) appears unless its block also holds a source link or citation.
One line next to the primary action answers the biggest reason not to click: cost, card, time, setup or data.
Section headings carry the argument on their own: reading only the headings explains the product.
Body copy scores Flesch–Kincaid grade 9 or below, or the record gives the audience reason.
No notes to the builder or the client reach the page: nothing like "the brief", "confirm with the client", "placeholder", "TODO", "lorem ipsum" or a bracketed "[Company]".
Every date shown with a weekday is a real date: the weekday matches the day, month and year.
The headline and primary action are visible without scrolling at 1440×900 and 390×844.
The primary action's label starts with a verb and names the outcome in 2–5 words; "Get started", "Learn more", "Start now" or "Try it now" alone fail. "Book a demo" and "Join the waitlist" pass.
The headline has no single-word last line at 390 or 1440.
A headline above about 6.5rem is the signature of the page and keeps each line to three words or fewer.
The first screen is not a false floor: at 1440×900 and 390×844 some content below the hero, or a hero element cut by the fold, shows in the bottom 15% of the viewport.
The hero is sized with svh/dvh or by its content, not a fixed 100vh that clips under mobile browser bars.

The signature artifact (marked `data-signature`) shows at least 280px of itself, or all of itself, within the first two screens at 390×844 and at 1440×900: right after the hero, not five sections down.
The 1440 first screen has no empty block of 320×140px or more, covering 8% of it, reaching the middle of the page: no action floating in an empty column, no hole above the headline.

The first screen is calm: at 1440×900 and 390×844, at most 60 words show outside the site header and the pictures (the hero picture marked `data-hero-visual`, drawings and anything hidden from assistive tech), not counting the next section peeking in at the bottom.
The first screen holds no table, form field, tab list or slider, at most two actions outside the header, and no controls inside the hero picture.
Cost is easy to find: a header or footer link to pricing or plans, or visible prices; otherwise the record says how cost is disclosed and why.
Within 5 seconds at 390×844, no dialog or fixed overlay covers more than 30% of the viewport, except a legally required consent prompt named in the record.

Clickable things look clickable: the primary action has a fill or a border with at least 3:1 contrast against its surroundings, and links inside paragraphs are underlined or differ from body text by at least 3:1.
Real proof, when supplied, appears within the first two screenfuls or beside the claim it supports, and every quote carries name, role and company.
The conversion form shows at most three fields before submit, no textarea and at most one select.
For developer products, the first two screenfuls show an install command or code sample, and the header links to docs or a quickstart; other products are n/a.

Every section after the first screen is understood at a glance: at most 90 words outside the demo, the pictures and closed details, so the heading and a line or two carry it and the details sit behind a disclosure, a table or another page.
Exactly one h1.
Heading levels never skip (no h1 → h3).
The h1 and the first h2 are each at least 1.25× the body size.
Headline letter-spacing is no tighter than −0.04em.
Body text is at least 16px on phones.
No readable text below 12px, superscripts and labels included.
Body paragraphs stay under about 80 rendered characters per line.
Body line-height is at least 1.35.
Weights under 400 appear only at 28px and up; smaller text is 400 or heavier.
A display face that is everywhere (Inter, Space Grotesk, Fraunces, Roboto, Poppins, Montserrat) has a stated reason, and every face has a role (display, text, data).
Every face renders as named for visitors: a named face is shipped with @font-face or is on every major platform, and never falls back to a browser default (Times, Arial, DejaVu, Liberation).
No horizontal scroll at 390px, at 1× and at 3× pixel density.
No horizontal scroll at 320px.
No text is cut off by its container.
Body text keeps at least 12px from the screen edge on phones.
No boxed card sits inside another boxed card.
In-page anchor targets and focused controls are never hidden under a sticky or fixed element, tabbing forward or back, at 1440 and 390.
A footer exists and holds real destinations.
A 200-character unbroken string typed into any text field and submitted causes no sideways scroll at 390px.
Buttons that sit side by side share their height and their vertical centre, within 2px, at 1440 and 390.
Text meets WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1, or 3:1 for 24px+ or 18.66px+ bold); text over images or gradients is sampled at its worst point.
No gradient-filled text and no coloured glow used as decoration.
The ground colour is chosen from where the product is used; cream with a serif display needs a reason.
Accent colour marks state or action and is not sprinkled for decoration.
No row of three equal cards with short adjective headings standing in for a product explanation.
No icon tile stacked above every card heading.
No small tracked-caps label above nearly every section heading.
No thick coloured side stripe on cards and no grid, dot or stripe background used as filler.
Replacing the logo would not turn this into another company's page, and the idea sentence fails with the nearest competitor's name in it.
Compared with each reference on copy, names, numbers, imagery, layout and motion, no distinctive element or combination is reproduced.
With reduced motion, nothing translates, scales or zooms and nothing is hidden; short fades are allowed.
After loading and one scroll, no text is still invisible.
No transition: all.
Only transform, translate, scale, rotate and opacity animate; never layout properties.
Nothing that moves or changes by itself runs longer than 5 seconds without a visible pause control, and the h1 and primary action never change by themselves.
Overshoot or bounce easing appears only in playful archetypes; entrances never start from scale(0) or ease-in.
Hover-only effects sit behind (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine), and staggers stay between 30 and 80ms without blocking input.
Every animation has a written contract: trigger, purpose, fallback, duration, easing.
The viewport meta never disables zoom.
On phones, the primary action and navigation controls are at least 44×44px.
Every other control is at least 24×24px or has enough space around it (WCAG 2.5.8); links inside sentences are exempt.
Inputs use at least 16px text, so phones do not zoom on focus.
If the nav collapses on phones, a working menu control replaces it, and without JavaScript the menu never covers the headline.
Dense artifacts are recomposed for phones, not shrunk or removed.
On phones, every control in the signature artifact answers in view: after a tap, something other than the control itself changes on screen, and no control is dead.
Escape closes an open menu and returns focus to the button that opened it.
On phones, controls inside the signature artifact are at least 44×44px.
The phone page is at most eight screens tall (6,752px at 390×844) and the signature artifact at most two (1,688px); a longer page cuts repeats and groups long lists.
The signature artifact asks for at most four decisions (a radio group counts once): one choice and one result, not a form.
Every link and button has an accessible name.
Every image has alt text, empty only when decorative.
Every focusable control shows a focus indicator from the keyboard: an outline at least 2px with at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colours.
Nothing is clickable without being a link or button.
Every form control has a label.
The html element declares a language and the page has a main landmark.
No script errors, console errors or malformed markup (an attribute left open by a missing quote) while loading.
Links point somewhere real: no empty href, "#" or missing anchor or file.
No broken images.
Results of local actions are announced (aria-live or role=status).
With WCAG 1.4.12 text spacing applied (line-height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2em, letter-spacing 0.12em, word-spacing 0.16em), no text is clipped or overlaps.
Using a signature-artifact control from the keyboard never drops focus to the page body (a control that disables itself hands focus on).
The first Tab stop (usually the skip link) is visible on screen when focused.
Images declare width and height or an aspect-ratio, and images below the first screen load lazily.
The largest element in the first screen (LCP) is not lazy-loaded or injected after load, and an LCP image has fetchpriority="high" or a preload.
Web fonts use font-display swap or optional.
Layout shift (CLS) through load, one scroll and one interaction stays at or under 0.1.
On a throttled mobile profile, lab LCP is at or under 2.5 seconds (a lab estimate, not field data).
The page has a title and a meta description; for an unknown brand the title leads with the category or audience.
Sharing works: og:title, og:description, an absolute og:image, twitter:card, a favicon and an apple-touch-icon are present, and theme-color matches the page background.
No customer logos or testimonials that were not supplied and verified.
Every number has a source or is labelled illustrative.
Illustrative interfaces and code are labelled right beside them, not in a separate disclaimer section.
Every action reaches what its label promises (install, docs, a real page or a visible local result).
No false urgency or scarcity: no countdown timer, "only N left" or "spots filling fast" unless it is true and sourced.
Every screenshot listed was opened, is not blank and is the width it claims, the 768 layout was looked at, and the signature artifact was captured in each of its states.
One structural revision was made after rendering, with before and after evidence and the hero rescored.
Every decorative element left on the page has a named job; ones without a job were removed and are listed.
The status line is DONE only if nothing above is unverified or unavailable; otherwise it names what is.
